summary: Plan of Arakelov geometry and heights of abelian varieties, Part II: adelic line bundles and arithmetic bigness on curve families. Starting where the parent roadmap stops (hermitian degree, ĈH¹ and heights of points), it plans the projective model theory of arithmetic intersection numbers, metrized Deligne pairings and arithmetic volumes; Yuan–Zhang adelic divisors and line bundles on quasi-projective schemes over ℤ or a field with their Berkovich analytification, intersection theory, volumes, heights, height inequality, fundamental inequality, equidistribution and invariant extensions; Moriwaki heights over finitely generated fields; Zhang's local admissible metrics on curves and their families (Yuan's canonical admissible bundles ω_{X/S,a}, O(Δ)_a and the canonical twice-theta bundle); the theta identities and nefness; the global ε, φ and Noether divisors; Yuan's bigness theorem for ω_{X/S,a} under maximal variation; potential bigness; and the uniform comparison of Zhang's admissible self-intersection with the stable Faltings height (Yuan Theorem 1.4).

nodes.title: Continuous hermitian line bundles on projective arithmetic varieties
nodes.statement: A projective arithmetic variety is an integral scheme X, projective and flat over Spec ℤ. A hermitian line bundle on X is a pair L̄ = (L, ‖·‖) of a line bundle L on X and a continuous metric ‖·‖ on L(ℂ) over the complex analytic space X(ℂ), invariant under complex conjugation. Its Chern current is c₁(L̄) = (1/πi)∂∂̄ log‖s‖ + δ_div(s) for any meromorphic section s. The metric is semipositive if c₁(L̄) is a positive current, and integrable if L̄ is isometric to a quotient of two semipositive hermitian line bundles. L̄ is nef if the metric is semipositive and the arithmetic degree of L̄ restricted to every closed integral curve of X (horizontal or vertical) is ≥ 0. Isometry classes form the group P̂ic(X) (tensor product), with subgroups P̂ic(X)_sm ⊂ P̂ic(X)_int; an arithmetic divisor is (D, g_D) with g_D a continuous Green function of D(ℂ) in the normalization g_D + log|f| continuous for a local equation f, and D̂iv(X) → P̂ic(X), (D, g) ↦ (O(D), ‖s_D‖ = e^{−g}) induces an isomorphism from arithmetic divisor classes. Over a field k the geometric analogue is a projective k-variety with ordinary line bundles, nef meaning nonnegative degree on curves.
hypotheses: X integral, projective and flat over ℤ; in the geometric case a projective integral variety over a field k.
Metrics are continuous (not necessarily smooth) and conjugation invariant.
Green functions use −log‖s‖, not −log‖s‖²: g_YZ = ½ g_GS.
proofSteps: Pass from smooth to continuous metrics: the regularity condition is local on X(ℂ) through local embeddings into complex manifolds (Yuan–Zhang §2.1.1).
Smooth metrics are integrable: twist by a high power of an ample bundle with a positive (pulled back Fubini–Study) metric.
Semipositivity on an ample bundle agrees with Zhang's notion of uniform limits of smooth semipositive metrics, by the regularization theorem of Coman–Guedj–Zeriahi cited in Yuan–Zhang §2.1.1 (1)–(3).
For X regular with smooth generic fibre and smooth metrics, (D, g) ↦ (D, 2g) identifies the arithmetic divisors here with those of ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights R35.1 §§1.8–1.9.
acceptance: On Spec O_K a hermitian line bundle is the hermitian line bundle of R35.1 §1.1 and the arithmetic divisor class group is the compactified Picard group of §1.7 (with g_v halved).
The trivial bundle with constant metric ‖1‖ = e^{−c} on Spec ℤ has arithmetic degree c.

nodes.title: Monge–Ampère measures of integrable metrics
nodes.statement: Let X be a complex projective variety of dimension n and L̄₁, …, L̄ₙ line bundles with integrable continuous metrics. There is a signed Radon measure c₁(L̄₁)···c₁(L̄ₙ) on X, multilinear and symmetric in the L̄ᵢ, positive when every metric is semipositive, of total mass the degree L₁···Lₙ, and continuous under uniform convergence of semipositive metrics. For a complete non-archimedean field the corresponding Chambert-Loir measures on X^an are those of TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic TB.6.
hypotheses: Complex projective variety, possibly singular; integrable continuous metrics.
proofSteps: Reduce to semipositive metrics by multilinearity.

Define the product of currents inductively by c₁(L̄₁)∧T = dd^c(log‖s‖ T) + δ_div(s)∧T on locally bounded psh potentials (Bedford–Taylor); continuity under uniform limits is their monotone convergence theorem, as cited in Yuan–Zhang §2.1.1.
Total mass is computed for smooth metrics by Chern–Weil and passes to limits.
acceptance: For the Fubini–Study metric on O(1) over ℙⁿ(ℂ), c₁ⁿ is the Fubini–Study probability measure.
On a curve, c₁(L̄) for an admissible metric is deg(L)·μ_Ar (GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights GZ.2).

nodes.title: Arithmetic intersection numbers of integrable hermitian line bundles
nodes.statement: Let X be a projective arithmetic variety and Z ⊂ X a closed integral subscheme of dimension d. For integrable hermitian line bundles L̄₁, …, L̄_d define L̄₁···L̄_d·[Z] ∈ ℝ inductively: for d = 0, [Z] = log #Γ(Z, O_Z); for d > 0 choose a nonzero rational section s_d of L_d on Z with div(s_d) = Σ aᵢZᵢ and put L̄₁···L̄_d·[Z] = Σ aᵢ L̄₁···L̄_{d−1}·[Zᵢ] − ∫_{Z(ℂ)} log‖s_d‖ c₁(L̄₁)···c₁(L̄_{d−1}). The value is independent of s_d and of the ordering, symmetric and multilinear; it satisfies the projection formula f^*L̄₁···f^*L̄_d·[Z′] = deg(Z′/Z)·L̄₁···L̄_d·[Z]; for Z vertical over p it is (L₁|_Z···L_d|_Z)·log p; for Z = Spec O_K it is the arithmetic degree. If every L̄ᵢ is nef the number is ≥ 0. For Z = X write L̄₁···L̄_d, a symmetric multilinear map P̂ic(X)_int^{dim X} → ℝ.
hypotheses: X a projective arithmetic variety; metrics integrable when Z is horizontal of dimension ≥ 2.
proofSteps: Independence of s_d and symmetry: Stokes/Poincaré–Lelong for the archimedean integral and the algebraic moving lemma for the finite part (the smooth case is Gillet–Soulé; continuous integrable metrics by Zhang's limit argument).
Projection formula and vertical case by induction on d.

Nonnegativity for nef bundles: perturb each bundle by a positive rational multiple of an arithmetically ample bundle. Arithmetic Nakai–Moishezon gives strictly small sections of sufficiently high powers of the perturbed bundles; induction gives nonnegative mixed intersections. Pass to zero perturbation by multilinearity and continuity of integrable metrics. No effective section of the original nef bundle is assumed (Yuan–Zhang §4.4.2 and Theorem A.4.1).
acceptance: For X = Spec O_K the number is deĝ(L̄₁) = log #(L₁/s O_K) − Σ_σ log‖s‖_σ (R35.1 §1.3).
For O(1) with Fubini–Study metric on ℙ¹_ℤ the self-intersection is 1/2 in the −log‖s‖ normalization (Gillet–Soulé value for ℙ¹).

sources.match: Gives the inductive definition, independence of choices, the projection formula, the vertical and arithmetic-curve cases, and the multilinear symmetric pairing on P̂ic(X). The positivity argument uses the arithmetic Nakai–Moishezon theorem recalled in §4.4.2, after ample perturbation.

nodes.title: The metrized Deligne pairing along projective flat morphisms
nodes.statement: Let f : X → Y be a projective flat morphism of relative dimension n between integral schemes (projective arithmetic varieties, or projective varieties over a field), and L₁, …, L_{n+1} line bundles on X. The Deligne pairing ⟨L₁, …, L_{n+1}⟩_{X/Y} is a line bundle on Y, symmetric and multilinear, compatible with base change, with ⟨…, f^*M⟩ ≅ M^{deg} (degree of L₁···Lₙ on fibres) and with deg⟨L₁, …, L_{n+1}⟩ = L₁···L_{n+1} when dim Y = 1. If the Lᵢ carry integrable continuous metrics then ⟨L₁, …, L_{n+1}⟩ carries a continuous integrable metric, equal to the fibrewise integral metric over the flat locus, with Chern current f_*(c₁(L̄₁)···c₁(L̄_{n+1})), semipositive when all metrics are; the pairing of nef (resp. ample) bundles is nef (resp. ample) in the geometric case, and of nef hermitian line bundles is nef. Over a non-archimedean place the analogous model metric is defined.
hypotheses: f projective and flat of pure relative dimension n. For the additional complex metric extension: f has finite Tor-dimension and pure relative dimension, and Y is normal; this extension agrees with the fibrewise metric only over the flat locus V.
Metrics continuous integrable.
proofSteps: Algebraic pairing: Deligne's construction via norms of rational sections, as recalled in Yuan–Zhang §4.2 following Muñoz García.
Metric: Yuan–Zhang Theorem 4.2.3, with continuity of fibre integrals from Theorem 4.3.1 (flat case, or normal base with unique continuous extension).
Positivity: Yuan–Zhang Lemmas 4.4.1–4.4.4 (degree on a curve base, nef and ample in the geometric case, arithmetic nefness).
acceptance: For n = 0 and f finite flat, ⟨L⟩ is the norm N_{X/Y}(L).
When dim Y = 1 over a field, the degree of ⟨L₁, …, L_{n+1}⟩ is L₁···L_{n+1} (Yuan–Zhang Lemma 4.4.1(1)).

sources.match: Constructs the continuous integrable metric on the Deligne pairing with fibral, base-change, symmetry, Chern-current and semipositivity properties; proves continuity of fibre integrals; proves the degree formula and nefness/ampleness of the pairing in the projective case.

nodes.title: Arithmetic volume, Hilbert–Samuel formula and the Siu inequality on projective models
nodes.statement: Let X be a projective arithmetic variety of dimension d and L̄ a hermitian line bundle. The set Ĥ⁰(X, L̄) of sections with sup-norm ≤ 1 is finite; put ĥ⁰ = log #Ĥ⁰. The limit vol^(L̄) = lim d!·ĥ⁰(mL̄)/m^d exists; L̄ is big if vol^(L̄) > 0. (1) If L̄ is nef then vol^(L̄) = L̄^d (arithmetic Hilbert–Samuel). (2) If L̄, M̄ are nef then vol^(L̄ − M̄) ≥ L̄^d − d·L̄^{d−1}·M̄ (arithmetic Siu inequality). (3) vol^ is continuous and homogeneous of degree d. The geometric analogues over a field hold with h⁰ = dim H⁰.
hypotheses: X projective arithmetic variety of dimension d (or projective variety over k).
Nefness as in AH.0/hermitian-line-bundles.
proofSteps: Finiteness of Ĥ⁰: a lattice intersected with a compact ball.
Existence of the limit and continuity: Chen and Yuan for smooth metrics, extended to continuous metrics by uniform approximation; recalled in Yuan–Zhang §5.2 (Theorem 5.2.1 proof).
Hilbert–Samuel: Gillet–Soulé arithmetic Riemann–Roch and Zhang's extension to nef, recalled in Yuan–Zhang Theorem 5.2.2 discussion.

Siu inequality: Yuan 2008 Theorem 2.2 proves, for ample L̄, M̄ and any Ē, χ_sup(Ē + N(L̄ − M̄)) ≥ (L̄^d − d L̄^{d−1}M̄)N^d/d! + o(N^d); since ĥ⁰ ≥ χ_sup asymptotically (Yuan 2008 §2, with h⁰ counting ‖s‖_sup < 1, which has the same volume), vol^(L̄ − M̄) ≥ L̄^d − d L̄^{d−1}M̄ for ample L̄, M̄, and for nef ones by approximation and continuity of the volume (Moriwaki, cited in Yuan 2008 p. 8; Yuan–Zhang Theorems 5.2.2 and 5.2.9).
acceptance: For L̄ = (O, e^{−c}) on Spec ℤ (d = 1), ĥ⁰(mL̄) = log(2⌊e^{mc}⌋ + 1), so vol^ = c = L̄ when c > 0.
Siu numerics: A nef big, B nef ⇒ vol^(A − εB) > 0 for 0 < ε < A^d/(d A^{d−1}B).

nodes.title: Model adelic divisors of mixed coefficients
nodes.statement: Let k be ℤ or a field and U a flat quasi-projective integral k-scheme. A projective model of U is a projective integral k-scheme X (flat over k when k = ℤ) with an open immersion U → X. Put D̂iv(X, U) = D̂iv(X)_ℚ ×_{Div(U)_ℚ} Div(U): pairs of an arithmetic ℚ-divisor on X (arithmetic divisors with continuous Green functions when k = ℤ; Cartier ℚ-divisors when k is a field) and an integral Cartier divisor on U with the same restriction. The group of model adelic divisors is D̂iv(U/k)_mod = colim_X D̂iv(X, U) over projective models, along pullback. It is partially ordered by effectivity (D ≥ 0 if on some model both the rational arithmetic divisor and the integral Cartier divisor on U are effective). The principal model divisors d̂iv(f), f ∈ k(U)^×, form a subgroup P̂r(U/k)_mod.
hypotheses: U flat, quasi-projective and integral over k.
Mixed coefficients: rational on the model, integral on U.
proofSteps: Pullback along a morphism of models dominating each other is injective on D̂iv(X, U) for models integrally closed in U (Yuan–Zhang Lemma 2.3.6–2.3.7).

nodes.title: The boundary norm and adelic divisors
nodes.statement: A boundary divisor of U is a pair (X₀, E₀) of a projective model X₀ and an effective Cartier divisor E₀ supported exactly on X₀ ∖ U when k is a field, or a strictly effective arithmetic divisor E₀ whose finite part has that support when k = ℤ. For D ∈ D̂iv(U/k)_mod put ‖D‖_{E₀} = inf{ε ∈ ℚ_{>0} : −εE₀ ≤ D ≤ εE₀} (∞ if no such ε). This is a norm in the sense ‖D‖ = 0 iff D = 0, ‖D₁ + D₂‖ ≤ ‖D₁‖ + ‖D₂‖, ‖aD‖ ≤ |a|‖D‖ for nonzero integers a, and two boundary divisors give equivalent norms. The group D̂iv(U/k) of adelic divisors is the completion of D̂iv(U/k)_mod for the boundary topology; a representative Cauchy sequence (Dᵢ) satisfies −εᵢE₀ ≤ D_j − Dᵢ ≤ εᵢE₀ for j ≥ i with εᵢ → 0, and its underlying divisor on U is eventually constant (and constant after discarding an initial segment).
hypotheses: A boundary divisor exists after blowing up; strict effectivity includes a strictly positive Green function in the arithmetic case.
proofSteps: Norm axioms and equivalence of norms: Yuan–Zhang Lemma 2.4.1, comparing E₀ and E′₀ on a common model.
Underlying divisors of a Cauchy sequence are eventually constant since ‖D‖ < 1 forces the integral part on U to vanish.
acceptance: For a nonzero boundary E₀, ‖E₀‖ = ‖−E₀‖ = 1; a divisor with nonzero integral restriction to U has norm ∞. For E₀ = 0 the norm at 0 is 0.

If U is projective over a field, take E₀ = 0: the topology is discrete. For projective arithmetic U, take E₀ = (0, 1): the norm of (0, g) is sup|g|, while nonzero underlying divisors have infinite norm. The model divisor group is complete in both cases, for different reasons.

nodes.title: The groupoid of adelic line bundles
nodes.statement: A rational hermitian line bundle on a projective model X is a pair (a, L̄) with a ∈ ℚ and L̄ hermitian (ordinary when k is a field); morphisms aL̄ → a′L̄′ are colim_m Isom(amL̄, a′mL̄′). An adelic line bundle on U/k is an integral line bundle L on U together with projective models Xᵢ, rational hermitian bundles L̄ᵢ on Xᵢ and isomorphisms ℓᵢ : L → L̄ᵢ|_U in Pic(U)_ℚ such that the model adelic divisors d̂iv(ℓᵢℓ₁⁻¹) form a boundary-Cauchy sequence. A morphism is an isomorphism ι : L → L′ with d̂iv(ℓ′ᵢ ι ℓᵢ⁻¹) → 0. This gives a groupoid P̂ic(U/k) with a forgetful functor to line bundles on U; isomorphism classes form the group P̂ic(U/k). Pullback along morphisms U′ → U of flat quasi-projective integral k-schemes and tensor products are defined termwise.
hypotheses: U flat quasi-projective integral over k.
proofSteps: Convergence and well-definedness: Yuan–Zhang §2.5.1 and Proposition 2.5.1.
Pullback: choose models of U′ over models of U; boundary divisors pull back to effective divisors bounded by a boundary divisor of U′.
acceptance: For U projective, P̂ic(U/k) is the groupoid of hermitian line bundles of AH.0 (integral coefficients).
The forgetful functor is surjective on objects when U has a projective model on which L extends.

nodes.title: Effective, strongly nef, nef and integrable adelic line bundles
nodes.statement: An adelic divisor is effective if it is a boundary limit of effective model divisors; an adelic line bundle class is effective if it is O(D) for an effective D. An adelic line bundle is strongly nef if it is isomorphic to an object (L, (Xᵢ, L̄ᵢ, ℓᵢ)) with every L̄ᵢ nef; nef if there is a strongly nef M̄ with aL̄ + M̄ strongly nef for all integers a ≥ 1; integrable if it is a difference of two strongly nef ones. P̂ic(U/k)_snef ⊂ P̂ic(U/k)_nef are semigroups and P̂ic(U/k)_int is a group; the same words apply to adelic divisors through O(·). nodes.title: Global Berkovich analytification
nodes.statement: Let k be ℤ (with the archimedean absolute value, a Banach ring) or a field with the trivial absolute value, and U a flat quasi-projective integral k-scheme. nodes.title: Density of divisorial points
nodes.statement: Let X be flat essentially quasi-projective integral over k and U a quasi-projective model. The map X^an → U^an is continuous and injective with dense image, and the points v ∈ X^an whose valuation on the function field is discrete or archimedean (with arbitrary positive rescaling) are dense in U^an. For S a positive-dimensional quasi-projective variety over a trivially valued field, points given by nontrivial discrete divisorial valuations of k(S)/k are dense in S^an; in dimension zero only the trivial valuation occurs.
hypotheses: k = ℤ or a field; dimension ≥ 1 for the divisorial statement over a field.
proofSteps: Reduce to the generic point (Spec F)^an ⊂ U^an and prove density fibrewise over M(k) (Yuan–Zhang Lemma 3.1.1(1)).

nodes.title: Effectivity is detected by Green functions
nodes.statement: An adelic divisor D ∈ D̂iv(X/k) is effective iff its analytification is effective. If X is normal, D is effective iff its total Green function g̃_D is ≥ 0 on X^an ∖ |D|^an. In particular, for an adelic divisor with zero underlying divisor, effectivity can be checked at the dense set of discrete or archimedean points of AH.2/divisorial-density.
hypotheses: X flat essentially quasi-projective integral over k; normal for the Green-function criterion.
proofSteps: Projective case: an arithmetic divisor on a normal model with nonnegative Green function is effective.
Pass to limits using the boundary norm; for zero underlying divisor apply continuity of g̃_D and density (Yuan–Zhang Lemma 5.1.2).
acceptance: For S = Spec ℤ, O(c) has total Green function tc at |·|_∞^t and zero on the non-archimedean rays; it is effective iff c ≥ 0.

nodes.title: Canonical measures of integrable adelic line bundles
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field or a one-variable function field over k, X a quasi-projective K-variety of dimension n, v a place of K and L̄₁, …, L̄ₙ integrable adelic line bundles on X/k. There is a signed Radon measure dμ_{L̄₁,…,L̄ₙ, v} = c₁(L̄₁)···c₁(L̄ₙ) on X_v^an, the limit of the Monge–Ampère (archimedean) or Chambert-Loir (non-archimedean) measures of the model metrics, positive for nef bundles. If X is projective, its total mass is the ordinary intersection number L₁···Lₙ; for projective X and nef L̄ of positive degree put dμ_{L̄,v} = c₁(L̄)ⁿ/(Lⁿ). On nonproper X, the degree and total-mass identity use geometric adelic intersections, as specified in AH.5/non-degenerate, rather than an ordinary degree of the uncompactified algebraic bundle.
hypotheses: X quasi-projective over a global field; bundles integrable.
proofSteps: Projective models: AH.0/monge-ampere-measures and TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic TB.6 model measures.
Boundary convergence gives convergence of measures on compact subsets of X_v^an (Yuan–Zhang §3.6 local theory and §5.4).
acceptance: For the canonical metric of a polarized dynamical system on ℙ¹ the measure is the canonical (equilibrium) measure of ArithmeticDynamics DY.4.

nodes.title: Canonical metrics over a trivially valued field
nodes.statement: For a projective variety X over a field K with the trivial absolute value, every line bundle L has a canonical metric on X^an, the model metric of L on X itself regarded as its own model over K. This prescribed model metric is called admissible in Yuan §A.6; for the curve bundles in AH.7 it is the specified trivial-valuation case (uniqueness refers to this model normalization, not to all continuous metrics with equal curvature), and it is used for ω_C and O(Δ) of a curve C over a trivially valued field.
hypotheses: K trivially valued; X projective over K.
proofSteps: For a point x ∈ X^an, properness gives Spec O_{H_x} → X. A generator of L near its reduction has norm one; this is independent of the generator, since transition units have absolute value one there (Yuan–Zhang §3.4.1). Tensor product and pullback preserve this prescription. A constant rescaling violates the normalization; no general curvature uniqueness assertion is needed.

nodes.title: The absolute intersection pairing of adelic line bundles
nodes.statement: Let X be flat essentially quasi-projective integral over k and d the absolute dimension of a quasi-projective model of X over k. The intersection numbers of AH.0/arithmetic-intersection-numbers (resp. geometric ones over a field) on projective models extend by boundary limits to a canonical multilinear map P̂ic(X/k) × P̂ic(X/k)_int^{d−1} → ℝ, symmetric in the last d − 1 variables and in all d variables when the first is integrable. If L̄₁, …, L̄_d are nef then L̄₁···L̄_d ≥ 0. For integrable L̄₁, …, L̄_d and a morphism f : X′ → X with the same absolute dimension, f^*L̄₁···f^*L̄_d = deg(f)·L̄₁···L̄_d (deg f = 0 if f is not dominant).
hypotheses: X flat essentially quasi-projective integral over k; d its absolute dimension.
proofSteps: For strongly nef L̄ᵢ represented by nef model sequences, the model intersection numbers form a Cauchy sequence: bound the change by the boundary norm times intersection numbers with E₀ (Yuan–Zhang Proposition 4.1.1).
Extend by multilinearity to integrable bundles, and to one non-integrable entry by the effective-boundary estimate.
Projection formula is the limit of the model projection formula (Proposition 4.1.2).
acceptance: For X = Spec O_K (d = 1) the pairing is the arithmetic degree on P̂ic(K/ℤ).
In the geometric case with X projective over k the pairing is the classical intersection number.

nodes.title: The adelic Deligne pairing
nodes.statement: Let Y be flat essentially quasi-projective integral over k and f : X → Y projective and flat of relative dimension n with X integral and Y normal. The metrized Deligne pairing of AH.0/projective-deligne-pairing extends to a symmetric multilinear functor f_*⟨·, …, ·⟩ : P̂ic(X/k)_int^{n+1} → P̂ic(Y/k)_int, sending strongly nef (resp. nef) bundles to strongly nef (resp. nef) bundles, and compatible with base change Y′ → Y by normal integral flat essentially quasi-projective Y′ with X ×_Y Y′ integral. For n = 0 and f finite flat it is the norm.
hypotheses: f projective flat of relative dimension n; X integral; Y normal.
proofSteps: Choose models f_i : Xᵢ → Yᵢ extending f; the model pairings of a Cauchy sequence form a Cauchy sequence for the boundary topology on Y because the pairing of a boundary-bounded divisor is boundary-bounded (Yuan–Zhang §4.5).
Nefness: limit of the model statement (Lemmas 4.4.x).
Base change: model base change plus Theorem 4.2.3(2).
acceptance: For Y = Spec F a finitely generated field, f_*⟨L̄₁, …, L̄_{n+1}⟩ ∈ P̂ic(F/k) is the vector-valued height of the generic fibre (Yuan–Zhang §5.3).
For dim Y = 1 projective over a field, the degree of the pairing is the intersection number on X.

nodes.title: Composition and projection formulas for the Deligne pairing
nodes.statement: Let ψ : X → Y and π : Y → S be projective of relative dimensions r and m between flat quasi-projective integral k-schemes, with π and π∘ψ flat and S normal; let L̄₁, …, L̄_{r+1} on X, M̄₁, …, M̄_{m+1} on Y and N̄ on S be integrable. (1) If ψ is flat and Y normal, (π∘ψ)_*⟨L̄₁, …, L̄_{r+1}, ψ^*M̄₁, …, ψ^*M̄_m⟩ ≅ π_*⟨ψ_*⟨L̄₁, …, L̄_{r+1}⟩, M̄₁, …, M̄_m⟩. (2) π_*⟨M̄₁, …, M̄_m, π^*N̄⟩ ≅ e·N̄ with e the degree of M₁···M_m on the generic fibre. (3) For d = deg_{X_η}(L₁···L_r) when ψ is dominant (and d = 0 otherwise): if ψ is flat and Y normal then ψ_*⟨L̄₁, …, L̄_r, ψ^*M̄₁⟩ ≅ d·M̄₁; without those extra conditions the always-defined composite pairing satisfies (π∘ψ)_*⟨L̄₁, …, L̄_r, ψ^*M̄₁, …, ψ^*M̄_{m+1}⟩ ≅ d·π_*⟨M̄₁, …, M̄_{m+1}⟩.
hypotheses: As stated; flatness of π∘ψ and normality of S throughout.
proofSteps: (1)–(3) are the limits of the model identities of Deligne pairings (Yuan–Zhang Lemma 4.6.1).
acceptance: With r = 0 and ψ finite of degree d, (3) says ψ_*⟨ψ^*M̄₁⟩ = dM̄₁.

nodes.title: Injective pullback and descent of fibrewise constant metrics
nodes.statement: Let π : X → S be projective flat with geometrically reduced and geometrically connected fibres between flat quasi-projective integral k-schemes. (1) π^* : P̂ic(S/k) → P̂ic(X/k) is injective. (2) Assume S normal or π has a section. If L̄ is integrable on X with L ≅ π^*M and on each fibre X_{H_v}, v ∈ S^an, the metric of L̄ is a constant multiple of the trivial metric induced by M, then M has an integrable adelic extension M̄ with π^*M̄ ≅ L̄.
hypotheses: π projective flat with geometrically reduced and geometrically connected fibres; for (2) S normal or π with a section.
proofSteps: (1) Proper flat finite presentation with geometrically reduced connected fibres gives π_*O_X = O_S universally (Stacks Tag 0E0L). The algebraic projection formula then makes Pic(S) → Pic(X) injective. Surjectivity of π^an detects equality of metrics, and full faithfulness of analytification gives the adelic assertion. Geometric connectedness alone is insufficient (source issue E3).

(2) Define the metric of M at v by the constant; continuity and adelic convergence from the Deligne pairing ψ_*⟨A, …, A, L̄⟩ with A relatively ample, using (3) of AH.3/projection-formulas (Yuan Lemma 2.1).
acceptance: If L̄ = π^*M̄ then the hypothesis of (2) holds with constant 1.
Connectedness alone fails: on E : y² = x³ + 3x + 2 over 𝔽₅, Frobenius is finite flat with geometrically connected nonreduced fibres, and kills the nontrivial order-five line bundle O((1,1) − O).

sources.match: States the injectivity and metric descent in Lemma 2.1. The injectivity assertion needs geometric reducedness in addition to its printed geometric connectedness; the corrected hypothesis holds for every smooth curve family used here (source issue E3).

nodes.title: Effective sections of adelic line bundles
nodes.statement: For an adelic line bundle L̄ on a flat quasi-projective integral k-scheme U, Ĥ⁰(U, L̄) = {s ∈ H⁰(U, L) : ‖s(x)‖ ≤ 1 for all x ∈ U^an}. If k = ℤ this set is finite and ĥ⁰(U, L̄) = log #Ĥ⁰; if k is a field it is a finite-dimensional k-vector space and ĥ⁰ = dim_k. Effective sections correspond to effective adelic divisors: s ∈ Ĥ⁰ ∖ {0} iff d̂iv(s) ≥ 0.
hypotheses: U flat quasi-projective integral over k.
proofSteps: Finiteness: normalize a projective model first. By AH.4/nef-domination choose an upper model divisor D̄′ on that normal model; bounded sections on U extend across the omitted prime divisors by their valuation inequalities. Hence Ĥ⁰(U,L̄) injects into the finite set (or finite-dimensional space) Ĥ⁰(X,O(D̄′)) (Yuan–Zhang Lemma 5.1.5). Normality is needed for this extension argument.
Identification with effective divisors by AH.2/effectivity-from-green.
acceptance: For U = Spec ℤ and L̄ = O(c), Ĥ⁰ = {n ∈ ℤ : |n| ≤ e^c}, ĥ⁰ = log(2⌊e^c⌋ + 1).

nodes.title: Adelic Hilbert–Samuel formula and Siu inequality
nodes.statement: Let X be flat essentially quasi-projective integral over k with absolute dimension d. (1) If L̄ is nef then vol^(X, L̄) = L̄^d; hence a nef L̄ is big iff L̄^d > 0. (2) If L̄, M̄ are nef then vol^(X, L̄ − M̄) ≥ L̄^d − d·L̄^{d−1}·M̄; in particular if A is nef and big and B nef then A − εB is big for all sufficiently small rational ε > 0. The same holds over a global field with d = dim X + 1.
hypotheses: L̄, M̄ nef adelic line bundles.
proofSteps: Strongly nef case: limit of AH.0/projective-volume-siu along representing sequences, by AH.4/adelic-volume.
Nef case: continuity of the volume function (Yuan–Zhang Theorem 5.2.9) applied to aL̄ + M̄₀ with M̄₀ strongly nef, a → ∞.

nodes.title: Positivity of Deligne pairings
nodes.statement: Let f : X → Y be projective flat of relative dimension n between flat quasi-projective integral k-schemes, Y normal of dimension d ≥ 1. (1) If L̄₁, …, L̄_{n+1} are nef and big on X then f_*⟨L̄₁, …, L̄_{n+1}⟩ is nef and big on Y. (2) If L̄₁ is effective integrable and L̄₂, …, L̄_{n+1} and M̄₁, …, M̄_{d−1} (on Y) are nef, then f_*⟨L̄₁, …, L̄_{n+1}⟩·M̄₁···M̄_{d−1} ≥ 0.
hypotheses: f projective flat, Y normal, dim Y = d ≥ 1.
proofSteps: (1) Put P = f_*⟨L̄₁, …, L̄_{n+1}⟩, which is nef. Choose a nef big model bundle M̄ on Y. Siu gives L̄₁ − εf^*M̄ big for small ε > 0, hence a positive multiple is effective. Pair it with the remaining nef entries to obtain a pseudo-effective Q. The projection formula gives P = Q + cM̄ with c > 0, since the remaining big bundles have positive mixed degree on the generic fibre. Compare successively P^d ≥ cM̄·P^{d−1} ≥ ⋯ ≥ c^dM̄^d > 0; each difference pairs Q with nef entries. This avoids multiplying several merely pseudo-effective bundles (Yuan Lemma 2.2).
(2) Composition formula AH.3/projection-formulas(1) reduces to an intersection number on X of an effective bundle with nef ones, ≥ 0.
acceptance: For n = 0 and f finite flat, (1) says the norm of a nef big bundle is nef big.

nodes.title: Bigness of nef bundles under finite covers
nodes.statement: Let S′ → S be a finite surjective morphism of flat quasi-projective integral k-schemes of the same dimension. A nef adelic line bundle M̄ on S is big iff its pullback to S′ is big.

proofSteps: By AH.4/hilbert-samuel-siu, bigness of a nef bundle is positivity of its top self-intersection; by the projection formula of AH.3/intersection-pairing the top self-intersection is multiplied by deg(S′/S) > 0 under pullback.

nodes.title: Domination by nef effective model divisors
nodes.statement: Let X be flat essentially quasi-projective integral over k and D an adelic divisor on X. There is, on a common quasi-projective model U, a model adelic divisor D′ induced by an effective nef arithmetic divisor on a projective model of U such that −D′ ≤ D ≤ D′. In particular every adelic line bundle is dominated by a nef effective model bundle.
hypotheses: X flat essentially quasi-projective integral over k.
proofSteps: Choose a model on which a representative of D lives; bound it above and below by multiples of an ample effective arithmetic divisor plus the boundary, then use that ample plus boundary is dominated by nef effective (Yuan–Zhang Lemma 5.1.7(1)).
acceptance: For U projective, D′ can be any sufficiently ample effective arithmetic divisor.

nodes.title: Heights of algebraic points for adelic line bundles
nodes.statement: Let k = ℤ and K a number field, or k a field and K a one-variable function field over k, and X a quasi-projective K-variety. For L̄ ∈ P̂ic(X/k) and x ∈ X(K̄) with closure x̃ (Spec of the residue field K(x)) put h_L̄(x) = deĝ(L̄|_x̃)/[K(x) : ℚ] (k = ℤ) or deĝ(L̄|_x̃)/[K(x) : K] (k a field), where deĝ is the adelic intersection number on Spec K(x) over k (residue degrees over the fixed k in the geometric case). This is Yuan's normalization: in the arithmetic case Yuan–Zhang §5.3 divide by the degree over K instead, so h_YZ = [K : ℚ]·h_L̄ (Yuan p. 64 records the difference); in the geometric case the two agree. More generally, for a finitely generated field F over k and X a quasi-projective F-variety, for integrable L̄ the vector-valued height h(x) = π_*⟨L̄|_x̃⟩/deg(x) ∈ P̂ic(F/k)_ℚ, and for H̄ ∈ P̂ic(F/k) satisfying the Moriwaki condition the real height h^H̄_L̄(x) = h(x)·H̄^{d−1}. h_L̄ is additive in L̄, functorial under pullback, invariant under Galois conjugation and independent of the field used to represent a point with K fixed. Under a finite extension K′/K, absolute arithmetic heights are invariant; geometric heights with degrees over the fixed k scale by [K′ : K], and for a model hermitian line bundle it is the metrized height of ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights R35.1 §1.12; for L̄ with trivial underlying bundle pulled back from P̂ic(K/k), h is the constant deĝ/[K : ℚ].
hypotheses: X quasi-projective over a global field K (or over a finitely generated field F).
proofSteps: Restriction of adelic line bundles to the closed point x̃ (pullback along Spec K(x) → X) and the degree map on P̂ic(K(x)/k).
Independence of the field of definition: projection formula for Spec K′ → Spec K(x).
Vector-valued heights and the Moriwaki condition: Yuan–Zhang §5.3.
acceptance: For X = ℙⁿ_K and L̄ = O(1) with the standard metrics (max at finite places, max or Fubini–Study at infinity), h_L̄ is the absolute logarithmic Weil height up to a bounded function (equal for max metrics).
Function-field normalization: ‖·‖_v = e^{−[k(v):k] ord_v} at places of K′.

nodes.title: The Yuan–Zhang height inequality
nodes.statement: Let k = ℤ and K a number field, or k a field and K a one-variable function field over k. Let π : X → S be a morphism of quasi-projective K-varieties, L̄ ∈ P̂ic(X/k), M̄ ∈ P̂ic(S/k), and L̃ the image of L̄ in P̂ic(X/K). (1) If L̄ is big on X/k, there are ε > 0 and a dense open U ⊂ X with h_L̄(x) ≥ ε·h_M̄(π(x)) for all x ∈ U(K̄). (2) If L̄ is nef on X/k and L̃ is big on X/K, then for every c > 0 there are ε > 0 and dense open U with h_L̄(x) ≥ ε h_M̄(π(x)) − c. (3) If L̃ is big, there are c, ε > 0 and U with h_L̄ ≥ ε h_M̄∘π − c. For a strict inequality outside a divisor (as needed for closed ≤ small-point sets), apply (1) to M̄ + Ā with Ā of strictly positive height.
hypotheses: As stated; K a global field.
proofSteps: (1) Bigness gives, for small ε, a nonzero effective section s of m(L̄ − επ^*M̄) (Siu, AH.4/hilbert-samuel-siu), and h_{L̄−επ^*M̄} ≥ 0 off div(s) (Yuan–Zhang Theorem 5.3.7).
(2)–(3) Add a small multiple of the pullback of a positive-degree bundle on Spec K, which makes L̄ big by Siu, then subtract.
Strict version: replace M̄ by M̄ + Ā where Ā has positive height everywhere (Yuan p. 65 with the correction recorded at PAPER-YUAN-26/E21).
acceptance: For X = S and π = id, (1) says a big L̄ has heights bounded below by a positive multiple of any height off a divisor.

Applies the height inequality to big adelic bundles; item PAPER-YUAN-26/121.

nodes.title: The fundamental inequality over global fields
nodes.statement: Let k = ℤ and K a number field, or k a field and K a one-variable function field over k; X a quasi-projective K-variety of dimension n; L̄ a nef element of P̂ic(X/k)_ℚ whose image L̃ in P̂ic(X/K)_ℚ is big. Put a_K = [K : ℚ] in the arithmetic case and a_K = 1 in the geometric case. With the absolute arithmetic normalization of AH.4/adelic-heights, h_L̄(X) = L̄^{n+1}/(a_K·(n+1)·deg L̃) and the essential minimum e₁(X, L̄) = sup_U inf_{x∈U(K̄)} h_L̄(x), one has e₁(X, L̄) ≥ h_L̄(X) ≥ e₁(X, L̄)/(n + 1).
hypotheses: L̄ nef on X/k; L̃ big on X/K.
proofSteps: First inequality: Hilbert–Samuel (AH.4/hilbert-samuel-siu) gives sections of m(L̄ − t) for t < h_L̄(X), whose divisors contain all points of small height (Yuan–Zhang Lemma 5.3.4).
Second inequality: successive minima argument of Zhang on a projective model, passed to the limit (Yuan–Zhang Theorem 5.3.3).
acceptance: For a point (n = 0), h_L̄(X) = e₁ = h_L̄(x).

Over a number field K and X = Spec K with O(c) pulled back from Spec ℤ, L̄¹ = [K : ℚ]c, deg L̃ = 1 and both h_L̄(X) and e₁ equal c. Omitting a_K would contradict the point case whenever [K : ℚ] > 1 and c ≠ 0.

nodes.title: Equidistribution of generic small points on quasi-projective varieties
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field (k = ℤ) or a one-variable function field over k, X a quasi-projective K-variety and L̄ a nef adelic line bundle on X/k with deg L̃(X) > 0. If {x_m} is a generic sequence in X(K̄) (no subsequence in a proper closed subvariety) with h_L̄(x_m) → h_L̄(X) (the consistently normalized variety height of AH.4/fundamental-inequality), then for every place v of K the Galois orbits of x_m equidistribute in X_v^an for the canonical measure dμ_{L̄,v} of AH.2/canonical-measures. For X projective and L̄ a model bundle this is Yuan's equidistribution theorem of ArithmeticDynamics DY.4.
hypotheses: L̄ nef; deg L̃(X) > 0; generic sequence with heights tending to h_L̄(X).
proofSteps: Variational principle: for M̄ in the kernel of P̂ic(X)_int → P̂ic(X/K)_int and small rational ε, apply AH.4/fundamental-inequality and Siu to L̄ + εM̄ (Yuan–Zhang Theorem 5.4.3).
Quasi-projective step: test functions are approximated by Green functions of zero-underlying adelic divisors, localized at v (Lemma 5.4.4).
acceptance: For the canonical metric of a polarized endomorphism of ℙ¹, it is the dynamical equidistribution of DY.4.

sources.match: Uses the equidistribution of Galois orbits of a generic small sequence to c₁(M)^{dim X}/vol.

nodes.title: Invariant adelic extensions of polarized dynamical systems
nodes.statement: Let S be flat essentially quasi-projective integral over k, π : X → S projective flat with geometrically connected fibres, f : X → X an S-morphism and L ∈ Pic(X)_ℚ with f^*L = qL for a rational q > 1. (1) There is a unique L̄_f ∈ P̂ic(X/k)_ℚ with underlying L and f^*L̄_f = qL̄_f, and f′^*L̄_f = q′L̄_f for every f′ commuting with f with f′^*L = q′L and q′ ≠ 0 (Yuan–Zhang Theorem 6.1.2). (2) If L is relatively ample over S, so that (X, f, L) is a polarized dynamical system, L̄_f is the boundary limit of the Tate sequence q^{−n}(f^n)^*L̄₀ for any model L̄₀; it is nef, strongly nef when S has an affine model, and lies in P̂ic(X/k) when L ∈ Pic(X), q ∈ ℤ_{>1} and f^*L ≅ qL integrally (Theorem 6.1.1). (3) For an abelian scheme A → S and a line bundle L rigidified along the zero section with [−1]^*L ≅ εL, ε = ±1, there is a unique adelic extension with [2]^*L̄ = 4L̄ (ε = 1) or 2L̄ (ε = −1); it is integrable and [m]^*L̄ = m²L̄ (resp. mL̄) for all m (Theorem 6.1.3); for symmetric relatively ample L it is the nef extension of (2) with f = [2].
hypotheses: f^*L = qL in Pic(X)_ℚ, q > 1; π projective flat with geometrically connected fibres.
Nefness only for L relatively ample over S (polarized dynamical system).
proofSteps: Choose a boundary divisor; the divisor of the isomorphism ℓ : L → q⁻¹f^*L is bounded by rπ^*E₀, so the Tate sequence is boundary-Cauchy with geometric rate q⁻ⁿ (Yuan–Zhang Theorem 6.1.1).
Uniqueness: two invariant extensions differ by a vertical bundle V with f^*V = qV and boundary-bounded, forcing V = 0 by injectivity of analytification (Theorem 6.1.2).
Nefness: limit of nef model bundles after twisting by the pullback of an ample bundle on a model of S.
acceptance: For the squaring map on ℙ¹ over S = Spec K, L̄_f is O(1) with the max metric at every place.
For an elliptic scheme and L = O(e), the canonical extension computes the fibrewise Néron–Tate height.

nodes.title: Non-degenerate subvarieties and non-degenerate adelic line bundles
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, S a quasi-projective K-variety, (X, f, L) a polarized dynamical system over S, Y ⊂ X a closed subvariety, M = L̄_f|_Y ∈ P̂ic(Y/ℤ)_{ℚ,nef} and M̃ its image in P̂ic(Y/K)_{ℚ,nef} (the geometric part over K). Y is non-degenerate if deg M̃(Y) = M̃^{dim Y} > 0, equivalently M̃ is big on Y/K, equivalently the measure c₁(L̄_f)^{dim Y} on Y_σ(ℂ) is nonzero for one (every) embedding σ : K → ℂ (Yuan–Zhang Lemma 5.4.4), and the same at non-archimedean places. For an abelian scheme over a smooth base this is full rank 2 dim Y of the Betti map at some point. More generally a nef adelic M̄ on Y is non-degenerate if M̃ is big on Y/K. Non-degeneracy is not bigness of M on Y/ℤ: a non-degenerate Y can carry a generic sequence of small points, and then M^{dim Y + 1} = 0. For an abelian scheme A → S and a generically finite ι : Y → A, non-degeneracy of ι does not depend on the symmetric relatively ample rigidified L.
hypotheses: K a number field; Y a closed subvariety (or Y with a generically finite map).
proofSteps: M̃ is nef, so deg M̃(Y) > 0 iff M̃ is big (geometric Hilbert–Samuel, AH.4/hilbert-samuel-siu over K).

deg M̃(Y) equals the total mass of c₁(L̄_f)^{dim Y} on Y_σ(ℂ) (Yuan–Zhang Lemma 5.4.4); for abelian schemes this form is the Betti form, whose top power is nonzero iff the Betti map has full rank (Dimitrov–Gao–Habegger Proposition 2.2 as cited by Yuan–Zhang).
Independence of L: Betti forms of two relatively ample bundles bound each other by positive constants.
acceptance: For S = Spec K, M̃ is L|_Y and deg M̃(Y) = deg_L(Y) > 0, so every Y is non-degenerate.

nodes.title: Height inequality and equidistribution on non-degenerate subvarieties
nodes.statement: Let S be a quasi-projective variety over a number field K, (X, f, L) a polarized dynamical system over S, Y ⊂ X a non-degenerate closed subvariety and B̄ ∈ P̂ic(S)_ℚ. (1) For every c > 0 there are ε > 0 and a dense open U ⊂ Y with h_{L̄_f}(y) ≥ ε·h_B̄(π(y)) − c on U(K̄). (2) If {y_m} is a generic sequence in Y(K̄) with h_{L̄_f}(y_m) → 0, then for every place v the Galois orbits equidistribute for dμ_{L̄_f|_Y, v}.
hypotheses: Y non-degenerate; K a number field.
proofSteps: (1) is AH.4/height-inequality(2) for Y → S and L̄_f|_Y (Yuan–Zhang Theorem 6.2.2).
(2) The existence of the sequence forces h(Y) = 0 by the fundamental inequality; apply AH.5/equidistribution (Theorem 6.2.3).

nodes.title: The adelic Hodge bundle of a family of curves
nodes.statement: Let S be quasi-projective, flat and integral over ℚ or ℤ and π : X → S a smooth relative curve of genus g > 1. The Hodge line λ_S = det(π_*ω_{X/S}) with the determinant L² metric (‖β‖²_nat = (i/2)∫_{X_s} β ∧ β̄ on π_*ω) extends to an adelic line bundle λ̄_S on S/ℤ. Through the canonical isomorphism λ_S ≅ det(e^*Ω¹_{J/S}) (JacobianChallengePartII JC6) the determinant L² metric equals the Faltings metric ‖α‖²_Fal = (i^{g²}/2^g)∫_{J_s} α ∧ ᾱ (Szpiro), so h_{λ̄_S}(s) = h_Fal(X_s), the stable Faltings height of the Jacobian in Faltings' normalization, for s ∈ S(ℚ̄).
hypotheses: π smooth of genus g > 1; S flat quasi-projective integral over ℤ or ℚ.
proofSteps: Comparison of metrics: Szpiro Lemme 3.2.1 as cited in Yuan Lemma 3.4, on the canonical isomorphism of JC6.

Adelic extension: Yuan–Zhang Theorem 5.5.1 constructs ω(S) with Faltings metric on an abelian scheme from the minimal compactification of the Siegel moduli (pullback of the ample Hodge bundle with its logarithmically singular metric, R35.5 §§5.0b, 5.3–5.4).
Height identity: Yuan–Zhang Theorem 5.5.1 (h = h_Fal), with Faltings normalization from R35.2 §2.7.
acceptance: For g = 0 nothing is defined; for an elliptic family (g = 1, outside the hypothesis) the analogous statement is R35.5 §5.9.
Normalization: the Deligne/Yuan–Zhang squared norm (2π)^{−g}|∫α∧ᾱ| gives h_Del = h_Fal + (g/2)log π (R35.2 §2.7).

nodes.title: Moriwaki polarizations and Moriwaki heights
nodes.statement: Let k₀ be a finitely generated field over ℚ of transcendence degree d. A polarization B = (B; H̄₁, …, H̄_d; τ) consists of a normal projective flat integral ℤ-scheme B, nef smooth hermitian line bundles H̄ᵢ on B and an isomorphism τ : ℚ(B) ≅ k₀. For a projective k₀-variety X and a line bundle L on X, the Moriwaki height h^B_{k₀,X,L} : X(k̄₀) → ℝ is defined modulo bounded functions by h(P) = deĝ(ĉ₁(L̄)·ĉ₁(f^*H̄₁)···ĉ₁(f^*H̄_d)·[Δ_P])/[k₀(P) : k₀] for a model (X → B, L̄) and the closure Δ_P of P; it equals the Yuan–Zhang vector-valued height of AH.4/adelic-heights paired with H̄₁···H̄_d. B is big if every H̄ᵢ is nef and big. For a field isomorphism ι : k₀ → k′₀ and B′ = (B; H̄; ι∘τ), h^{B′}_{k′₀} ∘ ι = h^B_{k₀}. For d = 0 (k₀ a number field, B = Spec O_{k₀}) it is [k₀ : ℚ] times the absolute Weil height class. The displayed denominator is relative to k₀, as in Moriwaki and Yuan–Zhang; division by [k₀ : ℚ] is needed to compare with AH.4/adelic-heights.
hypotheses: k₀ finitely generated over ℚ; H̄ᵢ nef smooth hermitian.

nodes.title: The height machine for Moriwaki heights
nodes.statement: With k₀, B, X as in AH.6/moriwaki-heights: (1) h^B_{L⊗M} = h^B_L + h^B_M; (2) for a quasi-finite morphism q : X → Y of projective k₀-varieties and M on Y, h^B_{q^*M} = h^B_M ∘ q; (3) h^B_L is bounded below off the stable base locus of L, and bounded when L = O_X; (4) (Northcott) if L is ample and B is big, {P ∈ X(k̄₀) : h^B_L(P) ≤ C, [k₀(P) : k₀] ≤ D} is finite for all C, D; (5) if L and M are algebraically equivalent and L is ample, then h^B_M(P)/h^B_L(P) → 1 as h^B_L(P) → ∞.
hypotheses: As in AH.6/moriwaki-heights; for (4) B big and L ample.
proofSteps: (1), (3), (4): Moriwaki Proposition 3.3.7(2)–(4), (4) proved in Moriwaki §4 (Theorem 4.3).
(2): Wazir Proposition 2(iv) as cited by Gao–Habegger (the smoothness assumption there is unnecessary; q generically finite suffices in Moriwaki Proposition 1.3(2)).
(5): the argument of Lang, Fundamentals of Diophantine Geometry Ch. 4, Proposition 3.3 and Corollary 3.4, with Moriwaki heights in place of Weil heights.

nodes.title: The Moriwaki Néron–Tate height
nodes.statement: Let A be an abelian variety over k₀ and L a symmetric ample line bundle. The limit ĥ^B_L(P) = lim 4^{−n} h^B_L([2ⁿ]P) exists for P ∈ A(k̄₀), is independent of the representative of h^B_L, is quadratic (ĥ^B_L([N]P) = N²ĥ^B_L(P)), ≥ 0, and vanishes on torsion; if B is big then ĥ^B_L(P) = 0 iff P is torsion. For k₀ a number field it is [k₀ : ℚ] times the usual absolute Néron–Tate height, with the relative Moriwaki normalization of AH.6/moriwaki-heights. It equals the height of the invariant extension L̄_{[2]} of AH.5/invariant-extension paired with H̄₁···H̄_d.
hypotheses: L symmetric ample; B big for the kernel statement.
proofSteps: Tate's limit for the bounded-error class (HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions RP.0 Tate limit).
Nonnegativity from boundedness below of the ample height; kernel by Northcott (AH.6/moriwaki-height-machine(4)) applied to the subgroup generated by P (Moriwaki Proposition 3.4.1).

nodes.title: Silverman–Tate and specialization with Moriwaki heights
nodes.statement: Let k₀ be finitely generated over ℚ with a big polarization B (the Hᵢ are nef and big). (1) For an abelian scheme 𝒜 → S over a regular quasi-projective k₀-variety with a projective compactification a symmetric relatively ample L = O(1,1)|_𝒜, and an embedding into ℙⁿ × S̄ as in HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions RP.0/silverman-tate, there is c > 0 with |ĥ^B_{𝒜_{π(P)}}(P) − h^B(P)| ≤ c·max{1, h^B_{S̄}(π(P))}. (2) For S a smooth projective k₀-curve and a section σ_x over a generically finite S′ → S, ĥ^B(σ_x(t))/h^B_S(ρ(t)) → ĥ_{K,A}(x) as h^B_S(ρ(t)) → ∞ (Silverman's limit with Moriwaki heights). Here h^B_S has degree-one normalization, and ĥ_{K,A}(x), K = k₀(S), is the geometric generic-fibre height normalized over K: if x is represented over K′ = k₀(S′), divide its K′-height by [K′ : K]. The comparison height on S̄ is attached to an ample bundle.
hypotheses: As in RP.0/silverman-tate and RP.0/silverman-specialization-limit, with Moriwaki heights over k₀.
proofSteps: Apply the Moriwaki height machine and the duplication estimate exactly as in the imported RP.0 proofs. Wazir’s preprint Theorems 0.2–0.3 (pp. 4–5) explicitly give comparison and the specialization limit over a finitely generated characteristic-zero field; Gao–Habegger §§A.2–A.3 supply the ample comparison and big-polarization scope. For a section only after a finite cover, apply the section theorem upstairs and divide the geometric height by the cover degree, using h_S∘ρ/h_{S′} → deg ρ.
acceptance: For k₀ a number field (d = 0) these are RP.0/silverman-tate and RP.0/silverman-specialization-limit.

nodes.title: Admissible metrics on abelian varieties
nodes.statement: Let A be an abelian variety over a complete field K with a nontrivial non-archimedean absolute value and M a line bundle on A. If M is even ([−1]^*M ≅ M), a continuous metric on M is admissible if the isomorphism [2]^*M ⊗ M^{−4} ≅ O_A identifies it with a constant metric; if M is odd ([−1]^*M ≅ M^{−1}) replace 4 by 2; in general require admissibility of the induced metrics on M ⊗ [−1]^*M (even) and M ⊗ ([−1]^*M)^{−1} (odd). Every M has an admissible metric on A^an, unique up to a positive constant (Tate's limit); it is integrable, and semipositive when M is ample.
hypotheses: K complete non-archimedean, nontrivially valued; A abelian variety over K.
proofSteps: Existence: Tate's limit of [2^n]^* of a model metric, uniformly convergent by contraction (Zhang 1995, Yuan §A.3).
Uniqueness: two admissible metrics differ by a continuous function φ with φ∘[2] = 4φ + c (resp. 2φ + c), forcing φ constant.
Semipositivity: limit of semipositive model metrics when M is ample.
acceptance: For an elliptic curve with good reduction, the admissible metric on O(e) is the model metric of the Néron model.

nodes.title: Admissible metrics on a curve and on its square
nodes.statement: Let C/K be smooth projective geometrically integral of genus g > 1 over a complete nontrivially valued non-archimedean field. Choose α ∈ Pic¹(C) (after a finite extension if Pic¹(C)(K) is empty), the Abel–Jacobi map i_α : C → J and the theta divisor θ_α. A continuous metric on a line bundle L on C is admissible if for some m ≥ 1 there is a line bundle M on J algebraically equivalent to an integer multiple of θ_α with an admissible metric and an isometry L^m ≅ i_α^*M. A metric on a line bundle on C² is admissible if its pullbacks along (x, id) and (id, x) are admissible for every x ∈ C(K′), K′/K finite. Every line bundle on C (resp. C²) has an admissible metric, unique up to a positive constant; the notion is independent of α and of the finite extension, and compatible with base change. For a symmetric metric on O(Δ) (Green function invariant under transposition) the pullback along (x, id) is a metric on O(x).
hypotheses: C smooth projective geometrically integral of genus g > 1; K complete non-archimedean.
proofSteps: Existence and uniqueness on C from AH.7/abelian-admissible-metrics via i_α, using that every degree-d bundle is algebraically equivalent to (d/g)·i_α^*θ_α in Pic ⊗ ℚ (JacobianChallengePartII JC3 theta pullbacks).
Independence of α: two Abel maps differ by a translation, and translates of admissible metrics are admissible.
On C²: use the biextension Picard comparison (JacobianChallengePartII JC4 axis-normalized Picard and pointed-square comparison) and admissibility of the Poincaré bundle.
acceptance: For C with good reduction, model metrics from the smooth model are admissible.

nodes.title: The canonical admissible measure on a curve
nodes.statement: Let C/K be as in AH.7/curve-admissible-metrics. There is a unique probability measure μ_a on C^an such that a metrized line bundle L̄ on C is admissible iff its metric is integrable and c₁(L̄) = deg(L)·μ_a. It is the normalized curvature c₁(i_α^*O(θ_α))/g of an admissible theta metric. If M on J is algebraically equivalent to zero with an admissible metric then c₁(i_α^*M̄) = 0. At split semistable reduction, μ_a = (1/g)·i_*(Σ_v g_v δ_v + Σ_e (1/(r_e + 1))δ_e) on the skeleton (GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights GZ.2/explicit-skeleton-measure).

Characterization: an integrable metric with c₁ = deg·μ_a differs from an admissible one by a metric with zero curvature, hence by a constant (Calabi uniqueness, AH.7/canonical-metric-pair step).

nodes.title: Zhang's canonical admissible metrics on ω_C and O(Δ)
nodes.statement: Let C/K be smooth projective geometrically integral of genus g > 1 over a complete nontrivially valued non-archimedean field. There is a unique pair of metrics, on ω_C and on O(Δ) over (C²)^an, both integrable and the diagonal metric symmetric, such that for every finite extension K′/K and x, y ∈ C(K′): (a) c₁(O(x)) = c₁(O(y)); (b) c₁(ω) = (2g − 2)c₁(O(x)); (c) ∫ g_Δ(x, ·)c₁(O(x)) = 0; (d) the residue map (ω ⊗ O(x))|_x → K′ is an isometry. Here O(x) carries the pullback of the diagonal metric along (x, id). These are Zhang's admissible metrics; both are admissible; their pairing on divisors with disjoint support is Zhang's admissible pairing (D, E)_a; the canonical isomorphism ω_C ≅ Δ^*O(−Δ) and p₁_*⟨O(Δ), p₂^*L̄⟩ ≅ L̄ (L̄ admissible) are isometries up to constants that the normalization (c)–(d) fixes; and Q = (id_J, i_α)^*P with admissible L gives q₁_*⟨Q, q₂^*L⟩ odd with an admissible metric. The pair descends from a finite Galois extension, which reduces existence to the pointed case.
hypotheses: g > 0 as stated by Yuan; the proofs of (b) and of the measure identification need g > 1 (source issues PAPER-YUAN-26/E8, E28), so this roadmap uses the pair for g > 1 and records g = 1 as a gap.
proofSteps: Uniqueness: Calabi uniqueness on curves — two integrable metrics with the same Chambert-Loir curvature differ by a constant (Yuan–Zhang 2017 [YZ1] Corollary 2.2), and (c)–(d) fix the constants (Yuan p. 106).

Existence: take admissible metrics (AH.7/curve-admissible-metrics); restriction of an admissible O(Δ) metric to the diagonal is admissible (Heinz Proposition 4.3 as cited, Yuan p. 112); the pairing with the diagonal is an isometry up to constant (pp. 113–114); the Poincaré Deligne pairing is odd (p. 114); then normalize.
Descent: uniqueness gives Galois invariance (Yuan §A.4).
Comparison with Zhang's graph construction: Yuan p. 106–107 (Zhang 1993 Theorem 4.6).
acceptance: Genus normalization: for g = 1, (b) says c₁(ω) = 0 and does not determine the measure; use a positive-degree bundle (Yuan p. 113 note).

nodes.title: Explicit graph formulas for the canonical metrics
nodes.statement: Let K be complete discretely valued with e_K = |ϖ|⁻¹, C/K of genus g > 1 with a K-point and split semistable reduction, Γ the dual graph of the minimal regular model with unit edge lengths, i : Γ → C^an and r : C^an → Γ the skeleton inclusion and retraction, K_C the canonical divisor of Γ, μ the admissible graph measure and g_μ its normalized Green function (GZ.2, TB.6). (1) ‖·‖_a(x) = ‖·‖_model(x)·e_K^{g_μ(r(x), r(x))} on ω_C, where ‖·‖_model comes from the relative dualizing sheaf of the minimal regular model. (2) For distinct geometric points x, y defined over K′/K, g_{Δ,a}(x, y) = (i(x, y) + g_μ(r(x), r(y)))·log e_K, where i(x, y) is the intersection of the two sections on the minimal regular model over O_{K′} measured as length and divided by the ramification index e(K′/K) — equivalently, measured with residue degrees and divided by [K′ : K], which is how Yuan p. 116 prints the normalization. Plain length divided by [K′ : K] is wrong when K′/K has residue degree > 1 (the extraction note on PAPER-YUAN-26/225).
hypotheses: Split semistable reduction with a K-point; unit edge lengths for the minimal regular model.
proofSteps: Compare curvatures: c₁(O_C(f)) = −i_*(Δf) for model potentials (Yuan Proposition A.4, TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic TB.6 model–metric Laplacian), so the corrected metrics have curvature deg·μ_a; check (c)–(d) of AH.7/canonical-metric-pair.
For (2), the finite-extension normalization uses the ramification index (source issue PAPER-YUAN-26/E3 and the extraction note on item 225).

nodes.title: Rescaling, good reduction and trivially valued fields
nodes.statement: Let C/K be smooth projective geometrically integral of genus g > 1. (1) Replacing |·| by |·|^a (a > 0) replaces the canonical admissible metrics by their a-th powers and Green functions by a times their values. (2) If C extends to a smooth projective model over O_K, the canonical admissible metrics on ω_C and O(Δ) are the model metrics of ω_model and O(Δ_model) on the smooth model and its square. (3) If K is trivially valued, the canonical admissible metrics are the canonical (trivial-model) metrics of AH.2/trivially-valued-canonical-metric. (4) At real places, the canonical metrics are those of GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights GZ.2 descended through complex conjugation.
hypotheses: g > 1 (see AH.7/canonical-metric-pair).
proofSteps: (1) Conditions (a)–(d) are homogeneous under |·| ↦ |·|^a.
(2) Model metrics on a smooth model have curvature the Dirac mass at the Gauss point, satisfy (c)–(d) by adjunction on the smooth model, and uniqueness applies.
(3) The trivial model is smooth; apply (2) with O_K = K.

nodes.title: Existence and uniqueness of admissible extensions
nodes.statement: In the setting of AH.8/admissible-extension, every line bundle L on W has an admissible integrable adelic extension, and two admissible extensions of the same L differ by π_W^*N̄ for a unique N̄ ∈ ker(P̂ic(S/k)_int → Pic(S)). hypotheses: As in AH.8/admissible-extension.
proofSteps: Abelian scheme: decompose L into even and odd parts up to torsion and take invariant extensions (AH.5/invariant-extension, q = 4 or 2).

Curves: choose α of positive relative degree d with Abel map i_α : X → J; the pullback Pic⁰(J) → Pic⁰(X) and Pic⁰⁰(J ×_S J) → Pic⁰⁰(X ×_S X) have torsion cokernel (JacobianChallengePartII JC4), so a power of L is i_α^* of an admissible bundle on J plus a bundle algebraically equivalent to a multiple of θ, and its pullback is admissible.

nodes.title: The canonical admissible bundles ω_{X/S,a} and O(Δ)_a
nodes.statement: Let k be ℤ or a field, S flat quasi-projective normal integral over k and π : X → S smooth projective with geometrically connected fibres of genus g > 1. (a) ω_{X/S} has a unique isomorphism class of adelic extension w = ω̄_{X/S,a} whose metric on every X_{H_v}, v ∈ S^an, is the canonical admissible metric of AH.7/canonical-metric-pair. (b) O(Δ) on X ×_S X has a unique isomorphism class of integrable adelic extension D = Ō(Δ)_a inducing the canonical admissible metric on every (X²_{H_v})^an. Writing ⟨A, B⟩ = π_*⟨A, B⟩: (1) the canonical isomorphism ω_{X/S} → Δ^*O(−Δ) is an isometry w → Δ^*(−D); (2) the canonical identification p₁_*⟨O(Δ), p₂^*ω⟩ → ω is an isometry p₁_*⟨D, p₂^*w⟩ → w. For a point s of S whose residue field is a global field, w|_{X_s} and D|_{X²_s} are Zhang's ω_{X_s,a} and O(Δ_s)_a.
hypotheses: g > 1 (Yuan states g > 0; the genus-one normalization is unproved, source issue PAPER-YUAN-26/E8).
proofSteps: Take admissible extensions (AH.8/admissible-existence-uniqueness); the defects in (1) and (2) are fibrewise constants, hence by AH.3/pullback-injective-descent are pullbacks β̄₁, β̄₂ of base bundles with trivial underlying bundle; twist ω′_a and O(Δ)′_a to cancel them (Yuan §2.2.3, with the corrected display of source issue E12).
Uniqueness from the torsor structure: the conditions (1)–(2) pin the base twist.

If x : S → X is a section, Q = (id_J, i_x)^*P on J ×_S X has a canonical integrable adelic extension Q̄ with [2]_X^*Q̄ = 2Q̄ ([2] acting on the J factor), whose fibre at β ∈ J is the admissible extension of the degree-zero class β on X.

nodes.title: Admissible section divisors and evaluation
nodes.statement: With π : X → S as above and a section x : S → X, put O(x)_a = (x, id_X)^*D, an admissible adelic extension of O(x(S)). For every admissible adelic line bundle L̄ on X: (1) the evaluation isomorphism π_*⟨O(x), L⟩ → x^*L is an isometry π_*⟨O(x)_a, L̄⟩ ≅ x^*L̄; (2) there is a canonical isometry π_*⟨O(x)_a, O(x)_a⟩ ≅ −π_*⟨O(x)_a, w⟩ = −x^*w.
hypotheses: A section x; L̄ admissible.
proofSteps: (1) The algebraic evaluation isomorphism exists. At v ∈ S^an its log norm is the integral of log ‖1‖_{O(x)_a} against c₁(L̄_v) (Yuan Proposition 2.7, pp. 33–34). Admissibility gives c₁(L̄_v) = deg(L_v)μ_a and the canonical Green normalization makes this integral zero. Full faithfulness then gives the isometry; pulling back only the ω pairing does not prove this for arbitrary L̄.
(2) Apply (1) to L̄ = O(x)_a: π_*⟨O(x)_a, O(x)_a⟩ ≅ x^*(x, id)^*D = x^*Δ^*D, and Δ^*D ≅ −w by the adjunction isometry (1) of AH.8/canonical-admissible-bundles; while π_*⟨O(x)_a, w⟩ ≅ x^*w by (1).
acceptance: For S = Spec K and x ∈ C(K): ⟨x, x⟩_a = −⟨x, ω⟩_a, Zhang's admissible adjunction formula.

nodes.title: Vertical orthogonality and the relative arithmetic Hodge index identity
nodes.statement: Let M be a line bundle on X of relative degree zero with an admissible extension M̄, and ι : S → J the section of the relative Jacobian it defines. (1) π_*⟨M̄, V⟩ = 0 in P̂ic(S/k) for every V ∈ P̂ic(X/k)_vert. (2) π_*⟨M̄, M̄⟩ = −ι^*Θ̄ in P̂ic(S/k)_ℚ.
hypotheses: M of relative degree zero with admissible M̄.
proofSteps: (1) The Yuan–Zhang arithmetic Hodge index theorem for curves over finitely generated fields gives a unique-up-to-base extension M̄₀ orthogonal to all vertical bundles; fibrewise it is the admissible (flat) metric, so M̄₀ = M̄ up to base twist, which does not affect orthogonality to vertical bundles of fibre degree 0 (Yuan–Zhang Theorem 6.5.1, 6.5.4).

(2) On the universal Jacobian, the self-pairing of the normalized Poincaré bundle is the negative canonical twice-theta bundle (Yuan–Zhang Corollary 6.5.5, p. 207). Pull this identity back by ι and use the compatibility of Deligne pairings with base change. A possible base twist of M̄ does not change its self-pairing because its relative degree is zero. No multiplication-by-two map on S is assumed.
acceptance: For S = Spec K: ⟨M̄, M̄⟩_a = −2ĥ_θ(M) (Faltings–Hriljac form of the Hodge index theorem, GZ.2).

nodes.title: Admissible theta pullback formulas
nodes.statement: Let π : X → S be as in AH.8, α a line bundle on X of relative degree d with an admissible extension ᾱ, i_α : X → J the Abel map x ↦ dx − α (JacobianChallengePartII JC2), w = ω̄_{X/S,a} and ⟨A, B⟩ = π_*⟨A, B⟩. In P̂ic(·/k)_ℚ: (1) i_α^*Θ̄ = d²w + 2dᾱ − π^*⟨ᾱ, ᾱ⟩. (2) ⟨i_α^*Θ̄, i_α^*Θ̄⟩ = d⁴⟨w, w⟩ + 4d³⟨w, ᾱ⟩ − (4g − 4)d²⟨ᾱ, ᾱ⟩, and (g − 1)⟨i_α^*Θ̄, i_α^*Θ̄⟩ = g d⁴⟨w, w⟩ + d²ι_α^*Θ̄, where ι_α : S → J corresponds to (2g − 2)α − dω_{X/S}. (3) For a section x and α = O(x) (d = 1, ᾱ = O(x)_a): i_α^*Θ̄ = w + 2O(x)_a + π^*x^*w and ⟨i_α^*Θ̄, i_α^*Θ̄⟩ = ⟨w, w⟩ + 4g·x^*w.
hypotheses: g > 1 (the paper states g > 0); d any integer for (1)–(2).
proofSteps: (1) Put N̄ = i_α^*Θ̄ − d²w − 2dᾱ + π^*⟨ᾱ,ᾱ⟩. For any section x, AH.8/relative-hodge-index gives x^*i_α^*Θ̄ = −⟨dO(x)_a − ᾱ,dO(x)_a − ᾱ⟩. AH.8/section-evaluation and bilinearity give x^*N̄ = 0. This argument is compatible with every normal flat base change. Apply it to S′ = X, where the base-changed family has the diagonal section: its evaluation is N̄ itself, so N̄ = 0. This proves the relative arbitrary-degree formula here, rather than assuming the narrower degree-one, field-valued JC3 theta identity supplies it.

(2) Expand with ⟨A, π^*N⟩ = deg(A)N and ⟨π^*N, π^*N⟩ = 0 (AH.3/projection-formulas); the fibre degree of d²w + 2dᾱ is 2gd². For the second identity insert ⟨M̄, M̄⟩ = −ι_α^*Θ̄ for M̄ = (2g−2)ᾱ − dw (AH.8/relative-hodge-index).
(3) Specialize (1)–(2) with AH.8/section-evaluation: ⟨O(x)_a, O(x)_a⟩ = −x^*w and ⟨w, O(x)_a⟩ = x^*w.
acceptance: Consistency check (verified): substituting ι_α^*Θ̄ = −⟨M̄, M̄⟩ into g d⁴⟨w, w⟩ + d²ι_α^*Θ̄ gives (g − 1) times the first expansion in (2).
Consistency check (verified): (3) is (1)–(2) at d = 1 with ⟨ᾱ, ᾱ⟩ = −x^*w and ⟨w, ᾱ⟩ = x^*w.

nodes.title: Theta identities for the canonical, difference and universal shift maps
nodes.statement: With π : X → S of genus g > 1, w, D and ⟨·,·⟩ as above, in P̂ic(·/k)_ℚ: (1) for i_ω(x) = (2g − 2)x − ω_{X/S}, i_ω^*Θ̄ = 4g(g − 1)w − π^*⟨w, w⟩ and ⟨i_ω^*Θ̄, i_ω^*Θ̄⟩ = 16g(g − 1)³⟨w, w⟩; (2) for j : X ×_S X → J, j(x, y) = y − x, j^*Θ̄ = 2D + p₁^*w + p₂^*w and p₁_*⟨j^*Θ̄, j^*Θ̄⟩ = 4g·w + π^*⟨w, w⟩; (3) for the universal shift τ : J ×_S X → J ×_S J, τ(y, x) = (y, y + (2g − 2)x − ω), with Θ̄_J = p₂^*Θ̄ and q₁ : J ×_S X → J, π_J : J → S: q₁_*⟨τ^*Θ̄_J, τ^*Θ̄_J⟩ = 16(g − 1)³Θ̄ + 16g(g − 1)³π_J^*⟨w, w⟩.
proofSteps: (1) AH.9/theta-pullback-formulas with α = ω, ᾱ = w, d = 2g − 2: d² + 2d = 4g(g − 1) and d²(d² + 4d − 4g + 4) = 16g(g − 1)³.

(2) Over the base X (first projection) the curve X ×_S X → X has the diagonal section and canonical bundle p₂^*w; apply (3) of AH.9/theta-pullback-formulas: x^*w becomes w and ⟨p₂^*w, p₂^*w⟩ = π^*⟨w, w⟩.
(3) Over the base J the Abel map with α ↔ ω − y has d = 2g − 2 and (2g − 2)α − dω = −(2g − 2)y, so ι_α^*Θ̄ = (2g − 2)²Θ̄; the second identity of AH.9/theta-pullback-formulas (2) gives the formula.
acceptance: All three coefficient computations were checked symbolically in this plan (see the reader).

nodes.title: Zhang's invariants of a polarized metrized graph
nodes.statement: A polarized metrized graph (pm-graph) of genus g ≥ 1 is a compact connected metric graph Γ (TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic TB.3) with a vertex genus function q ≥ 0 such that b₁(Γ) + Σ q(x) = g and whose canonical divisor K = Σ_x (v(x) − 2 + 2q(x))x (v the valence) is effective (no genus-zero point of valence one); K has degree 2g − 2; μ = μ_ad is Zhang's admissible measure, g_μ its normalized Green function (GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights GZ.2, TB.6) and r the effective resistance. Define: δ(Γ) = ℓ(Γ) the total length, δᵢ(Γ) the total length of edges of type i (type 0: non-separating; type i ≥ 1: separating into parts of genus i and g − i); ε(Γ) = ∫∫ r(x, y)δ_K(x)μ(y); φ(Γ) = −ℓ(Γ)/4 + (1/4)∫ g_μ(x, x)((10g + 2)μ − δ_K); τ(Γ) the Baker–Rumely constant, g_{μ_can}(x, y) = −r(x, y)/2 + τ(Γ) for the canonical (possibly signed) measure μ_can of total mass one.
hypotheses: Γ compact connected metric graph with a genus function q ≥ 0 and effective canonical divisor; g ≥ 1 (g ≥ 2 for the curve applications).
proofSteps: μ_ad, g_μ and the Green-function identities are imported from GZ.2 and TB.6; the formulas for ε and φ are Zhang 2010 §4.1 and (4.1.4), τ is Baker–Rumely §14.
acceptance: One-loop graph (one vertex of genus g − 1 with a loop of length ℓ): μ = ((g − 1)δ_v + dx/ℓ)/g, K = (2g − 2)v, r(v, t) = t(ℓ − t)/ℓ, so ε = (2g − 2)·(1/g)·(ℓ/6) = (g − 1)ℓ/(3g); τ = ℓ/12; and by the de Jong identity φ = (g − 1)ℓ/(6g).
A single vertex of genus g with no edges has ℓ = ε = φ = τ = 0.

nodes.title: Inequalities between graph invariants
nodes.statement: For a pm-graph Γ of genus g ≥ 2: (1) r(x, y) is at most the length of any path from x to y, hence ≤ ℓ(Γ); (2) ε(Γ) ≤ (2g − 2)ℓ(Γ); (3) (Cinkir) φ(Γ) ≥ t(g)δ₀(Γ) + Σ_{i≥1} (2i(g − i)/g)δᵢ(Γ) with t(2) = 1/27, t(3) = (892 − 11√79)/14580 ≈ 0.0545, t(g) = (g − 1)²/(2g(7g + 5)) for g ≥ 4 (≥ 3/88), so φ(Γ) ≥ ℓ(Γ)/39; more precisely φ ≥ c(g)δ with c(2) = 1/27, c(4) = 3/88, c(g) ≥ 1/25 for g ≥ 5 and c(g) → 1/14; (4) τ(Γ) = ¼∫(∂_x r(x, y))²dx ≥ 0; (5) δ + ε − 2φ = (3/2)δ − 6τ, hence ε ≤ δ/2 + 2φ.
hypotheses: g ≥ 2; Γ a pm-graph.
proofSteps: (1) Rayleigh monotonicity: r(x, w) ≤ r(x, z) + r(z, w) (with the variable names of source issue PAPER-YUAN-26/E4) and r ≤ edge length on an edge (Baker–Faber §6, Klein–Randić Theorem D as cited by Yuan).
(2) ε = ∫∫ r δ_K μ ≤ (deg K)·max r ≤ (2g − 2)ℓ, since K is effective (part of the definition of a pm-graph) and μ is a probability measure (Yuan p. 48).
(3) Cinkir arXiv v2 Theorem 2.9 (Yuan cites it as [Cin1, Thm. 2.11]); min_g t(g) = t(4) = 3/88 > 1/39 and 2i(g − i)/g ≥ 1.
(4) Baker–Rumely Lemma 14.4. (5) de Jong Proposition 9.2.
acceptance: One-loop graph: ε = (g − 1)ℓ/(3g) ≤ (2g − 2)ℓ; φ = (g − 1)ℓ/(6g) ≥ ℓ/12 ≥ ℓ/39; δ + ε − 2φ = ℓ and (3/2)δ − 6τ = ℓ.

nodes.title: The local φ-invariant of a curve over a complete field
nodes.statement: For C smooth projective geometrically connected of genus g > 1 over a complete valued field K (archimedean via C_ℂ), with Zhang's admissible metrics (AH.7, GZ.2), φ(C) = −∫_{(C×C)^an} g_{Δ,a} c₁(O(Δ)_a)². (1) Non-archimedean, split semistable reduction, |ϖ| = e^{−1}, unit-edge reduction graph Γ: φ(C) = φ(Γ) of AH.10/polarized-graph-invariants. (2) Archimedean: with an L²-orthonormal basis ω₁, …, ω_g of H⁰(C, ω) for (i/2)∫α∧β̄ and an orthonormal eigenbasis φ_λ of the Arakelov Laplacian, φ(C) = Σ_{λ>0} Σ_{j,k} (2/λ)|∫_C φ_λ ω_j ∧ ω̄_k|², so φ(C) > 0. (3) φ(C) ≥ 0 at non-archimedean places. Under a finite extension K′/K with the extended absolute value, φ is unchanged; with |ϖ| = e^{−1} renormalized on K′, φ is multiplied by e(K′/K) (Yuan p. 49 prints the field degree [K′ : K] in the analogous rule for δ; PAPER-YUAN-26/E3).
proofSteps: (1) Integrate the explicit graph formulas of AH.7/graph-formulas (Zhang 2010 Theorem 1.3.1 and Lemma 3.5.4; finite-extension normalization by ramification index, source issue E3).
(2) Spectral expansion of the Arakelov Green function (Zhang 2010 Proposition 2.5.3); positivity since each term is ≥ 0 and not all vanish.
(3) From AH.10/graph-invariant-inequalities(3).
acceptance: Good reduction: φ = 0.
One-node degeneration of type 0 with thickness m: φ = (g − 1)m/(6g).

nodes.title: The global ε divisor E_S
nodes.statement: Let k be a field, S quasi-projective normal integral over k, π : X → S smooth of genus g > 1 with a stable compactification π̄ : X̄ → S̄ (StableReductionPartII MC.6). With P = π_*⟨w, w⟩, the canonical trivialization over S of π̄_*⟨ω̄, ω̄⟩ − P (both have underlying bundle π_*⟨ω, ω⟩ on S) defines an adelic divisor E_S ∈ D̂iv(S/k) with zero underlying divisor and O(E_S) = π̄_*⟨ω̄, ω̄⟩ − P. At a point v ∈ S^an given by a discrete valuation of k(S)/k with e_v = |ϖ_v|⁻¹ and polarized reduction graph Γ_v, its Green function is g_{E_S}(v) = ε(Γ_v) log e_v.
hypotheses: k a field; stable compactification exists (after a finite cover, MC.6/stable-compactification-exists).
proofSteps: Both bundles are adelic extensions of π_*⟨ω, ω⟩; their difference has a canonical section 1 over S.
Green function at discrete v: Zhang's formula ω_a² = ω²_model − ε (Zhang 1993 Theorem 4.4, recalled in Yuan p. 47) applied to X_{H_v}.
acceptance: If X̄ → S̄ is smooth (no boundary) then E_S = 0.

nodes.title: The boundary bound for the ε divisor
nodes.statement: In the setting of AH.10/epsilon-divisor, (2g − 2)Δ_S − E_S is an effective adelic divisor with zero underlying divisor on S, where Δ_S is the boundary divisor of the stable compactification restricted as an adelic divisor on S (its Green function at discrete v is ℓ(Γ_v) log e_v).
hypotheses: As in AH.10/epsilon-divisor.
proofSteps: By AH.2/effectivity-from-green and AH.2/divisorial-density it suffices to compare Green functions at discrete valuations: g_{Δ_S}(v)/log e_v = ℓ(Γ_v) (boundary multiplicity = node thickness, StableReductionPartII MC.5/boundary-thickness), and ε(Γ_v) ≤ (2g − 2)ℓ(Γ_v) (AH.10/graph-invariant-inequalities(2)).
acceptance: Consistency: for a one-node degeneration (g − 1)m/(3g) ≤ (2g − 2)m.

nodes.title: The global φ divisor Φ_S
nodes.statement: Let k be ℤ or a field, S flat quasi-projective normal integral over k, π : X → S smooth of genus g > 1, P = π_*⟨w, w⟩ and D = Ō(Δ)_a. Using the canonical algebraic identification (π, π)_*⟨O(Δ), O(Δ), O(Δ)⟩ ≅ π_*⟨ω, ω⟩, define Φ_S ∈ D̂iv(S/k) as the adelic divisor of the corresponding trivializing section of P − (π, π)_*⟨D, D, D⟩; its underlying divisor is 0. At a discrete or archimedean v ∈ S^an its Green function is ∫_{((X×_S X)_v)^an} log‖1‖_{Δ,a} c₁(O(Δ)_a)² = φ(X_{H_v}) (domain of integration corrected by source issue PAPER-YUAN-26/E2), in the normalization e_v = e and its rescaling for other norms.
hypotheses: g > 1; S normal.
proofSteps: Algebraic identification of the triple self-pairing of the diagonal with π_*⟨ω, ω⟩ by adjunction twice.
Green function: the metric of P − (π,π)_*⟨D,D,D⟩ at v is computed fibrewise by the Deligne pairing metric (AH.0/projective-deligne-pairing) and equals the local φ integral (Yuan §3.3.2).
acceptance: For S = Spec O_K[1/N] and a curve with good reduction outside N, the Green function at an archimedean place is φ(C_σ).

nodes.title: The triple self-pairing of the difference map
nodes.statement: With j : X ×_S X → J, j(x, y) = y − x, and Θ̄ canonical: (π, π)_*⟨j^*Θ̄, j^*Θ̄, j^*Θ̄⟩ = (12g − 4)P − 8O(Φ_S) in P̂ic(S/k)_ℚ. Writing wᵢ = pᵢ^*w and B(A, B, C) = (π, π)_*⟨A, B, C⟩, the expansion uses B(wᵢ, wᵢ, wᵢ) = 0, B(w₁, w₁, w₂) = B(w₂, w₂, w₁) = (2g − 2)P, B(D, wᵢ, w_j) = P, B(D, D, wᵢ) = −P and B(D, D, D) = P − O(Φ_S).
proofSteps: Expand (2D + w₁ + w₂)³ by multilinearity: 8B(D,D,D) + 12B(D,D,w₁ + w₂) + 6B(D, w₁ + w₂, w₁ + w₂) + B((w₁ + w₂)³).
Each auxiliary identity follows from AH.3/projection-formulas and the isometries of AH.8/canonical-admissible-bundles (B(D, D, wᵢ) = −P by adjunction; B(D, wᵢ, w_j) = P by the pairing isometry).
Sum: (8P − 8Φ) − 24P + 24P + 12(g − 1)P = (12g − 4)P − 8Φ (checked in this plan).
acceptance: Coefficient check: 8 − 24 + 24 + 12(g − 1) = 12g − 4.

nodes.title: Hodge lower decomposition of ⟨ω_a, ω_a⟩
nodes.statement: Let k be a field, S quasi-projective normal integral over k, π : X → S smooth of genus g > 1 with a stable compactification. In P̂ic(S)_ℚ, P = π_*⟨w, w⟩ = (3/(5(2g − 1)(3g − 1)))λ_S̄ + A + O(B) with A nef and B effective with zero underlying divisor, where λ_S̄ is the Hodge line of the compactification.
hypotheses: k a field; stable compactification.
proofSteps: P = π̄_*⟨ω̄, ω̄⟩ − O(E_S) = 12λ − O(E_S + Δ_S) (universal Noether formula pulled back, StableReductionPartII MC.5/integral-noether) = 12λ − (2g − 1)O(Δ_S) + eff (AH.10/epsilon-bound).
P = (2/(3g − 1))O(Φ_S) + nef (AH.10/triple-pairing with j^*Θ̄ nef: (12g − 4)P − 8O(Φ_S) is nef) = (2/(39(3g − 1)))O(Δ_S) + nef + eff (AH.10/phi-bound).
Cancel Δ_S: (1 + 39(3g − 1)(2g − 1)/2)P = 12λ + nef + eff; replace the coefficient by 20(3g − 1)(2g − 1) ≥ it (allowed since P is nef, AH.9/nefness-omega-a), giving 3/(5(2g − 1)(3g − 1)).

sources.match: Proves the decomposition P = 3λ/(5(2g − 1)(3g − 1)) + nef + effective by combining Noether, the ε bound, the triple pairing and the φ bound; item PAPER-YUAN-26/105.

nodes.title: The Gross–Schoen height and its adelic variation
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field or one-variable function field and C/K smooth projective geometrically connected of genus g > 1; choose a rational degree-one divisor ξ = Σ aᵢpᵢ with (2g − 2)ξ = ω_C. The modified diagonal Δ_ξ = Δ₁₂₃ − Δ₁₂ − Δ₂₃ − Δ₃₁ + Δ₁ + Δ₂ + Δ₃ ∈ CH²(C³)_ℚ (Δ₁₂ = Σ aᵢ{(x, x, pᵢ)}, Δ₁ = Σ aᵢa_j{(x, pᵢ, p_j)}, and permutations) is homologically trivial, and its Gross–Schoen (Beilinson–Bloch) self-height satisfies ⟨Δ_ξ, Δ_ξ⟩ = ((2g + 1)/(2g − 2))ω_a² − Σ_v φ(C_v)deg(v) (Zhang). For a smooth family π : X → S over a quasi-projective normal K-variety, L = ((2g + 1)/(2g − 2))π_*⟨w, w⟩ − O(Φ_S) ∈ P̂ic(S/k)_ℚ satisfies h_L(y) = ⟨Δ_ξ(X_y), Δ_ξ(X_y)⟩/a_y for y ∈ S(K̄), where the pairing in the numerator uses the raw local sums over K(y), and a_y = [K(y) : ℚ] for number fields or [K(y) : K] for function fields. This is the normalized fibrewise Gross–Schoen height; the displayed single-curve identity uses raw intersections and raw local sums on both sides. No nefness or bigness of L is asserted.
hypotheses: g > 1; ξ exists after a finite extension of K.
proofSteps: Homological triviality of Δ_ξ and the Gross–Schoen regular-model construction of its height (Gross–Schoen 1995, as recalled in Zhang 2010 §1.1).
Zhang 2010 Theorem 1.3.1 with x_ξ = 0 (the extra term 6(g − 1)⟨x_ξ, x_ξ⟩ vanishes since (2g − 2)ξ = ω).
Family version: restrict L to y and use AH.4/adelic-heights with AH.10/phi-divisor (Yuan §3.3.5).
acceptance: If C is hyperelliptic then ⟨Δ_ξ, Δ_ξ⟩ = 0, giving ω_a² = ((2g − 2)/(2g + 1))Σφ (AH.13/phi-lower-bounds).

sources.match: Defines the Gross–Schoen modified diagonal for a degree-one divisor and proves the height formula in terms of ω_a² and local φ-invariants.
Recalls the Gross–Schoen cycle and formula and defines the adelic line bundle L whose height is the Gross–Schoen height; items PAPER-YUAN-26/102–104, 257.

nodes.title: Faltings' δ-invariant
nodes.statement: For a compact connected Riemann surface X of genus g ≥ 1, Faltings' δ(X) ∈ ℝ is the constant in Faltings' comparison of the Arakelov metric on det H⁰(X, ω) with ‖θ‖ and Arakelov Green functions (Faltings 1984, p. 401–402). Fix a period matrix Ω with Y = Im Ω, θ(z,Ω) = Σ_{n∈ℤ^g} exp(πi nᵗΩn + 2πi nᵗz), ‖θ‖(z) = (det Y)^{1/4} exp(−π(Im z)ᵗY⁻¹(Im z))|θ(z,Ω)|, and ν = (i/2)Σ_{j,k}(Y⁻¹)_{jk}dz_j ∧ d z̄_k, transported to Pic^{g−1}(X) through its theta divisor; ∫ν^g/g! = 1. Equivalently (Wilms Theorem 1.1) δ(X) = −24∫_{Pic^{g−1}(X)} log‖θ‖ ν^g/g! + 2φ(X) − 8g log 2π. For a semistable curve over a number field, the global δ(C) = Σ_{v finite} δ_v log Nv + Σ_σ δ(C_σ), with δ_v the number of singular points of the geometric special fibre of the minimal regular model at v.
hypotheses: g ≥ 1 (g > 1 in the applications).
proofSteps: Definition by Faltings; Wilms' formula as a characterisation (Wilms Theorem 1.1).
acceptance: g = 1: φ = 0 and δ is −24∫log‖θ‖ − 8 log 2π, with δ > −9 (Faltings §7 as recalled by Wilms).

nodes.title: The arithmetic Noether formula
nodes.statement: For C/K smooth projective geometrically connected of genus g > 1 over a number field with semistable minimal regular model 𝒞 over O_K, 12 deĝ(λ̄) = ω²_{𝒞,Ar} + δ(C) − 4g[K : ℚ]log(2π), where λ̄ = det π_*ω with the determinant L² metric (AH.5/adelic-hodge-bundle), ω_{𝒞,Ar} the relative dualizing sheaf with the Arakelov metric (GZ.2) and δ(C) the global δ-invariant.
hypotheses: Semistable minimal regular model over O_K; g > 1.
proofSteps: Faltings, Calculus on arithmetic surfaces, Theorem 6, with the constant corrected by Moret-Bailly, La formule de Noether pour les surfaces arithmétiques, Théorème 2.5 (as cited by Yuan p. 89). The proof via the Deligne pairing and the Quillen metric is not repeated here; see the gap list.

nodes.title: The admissible Noether divisor Ξ_S
nodes.statement: Let k be ℤ or ℚ, S flat quasi-projective normal integral over k, π : X → S smooth of genus g > 1. The semi-canonical Noether isomorphism 12λ_S ≅ π_*⟨ω, ω⟩ (on S, where Δ_S is empty; StableReductionPartII MC.5/semi-canonical-noether), unique up to sign, defines Ξ_S ∈ D̂iv(S/k) with zero underlying divisor and O(Ξ_S) = 12λ̄_S − π_*⟨w, w⟩; it is independent of the sign. Its Green function is δ_v + ε_v at a normalized discrete v and δ(X_v) − 4g log(2π) at a normalized archimedean v. If the rational-base family has a stable compactification, the image of Ξ_S in D̂iv(S_ℚ/ℚ) is E_{S_ℚ} + Δ_{S_ℚ}.
hypotheses: k = ℤ or ℚ; g > 1.
proofSteps: Define Ξ_S as the divisor of the semi-canonical section of 12λ̄_S − π_*⟨w, w⟩; the sign ambiguity does not change the divisor of a section (|−s| = |s|).

Local Green functions: at discrete v, compare with Zhang's ω_a² = ω²_model − ε and the local Noether formula (δ_v nodes); at archimedean v, the arithmetic Noether formula AH.10/arithmetic-noether fibrewise.
Geometric part: compare with AH.10/epsilon-divisor and the universal Noether formula.
acceptance: Over a single curve with good reduction at v, the Green function at v is 0.
